title: 1981 AHSME Problem 13
statement: Suppose that at the end of any year, a unit of money has lost \(10\%\) of the value it had at the beginning of that year. Find the smallest integer \(n\) such that after \(n\) years the unit of money will have lost at least \(90\%\) of its value. (To the nearest thousandth \(\log_{10}3\) is \(0.477.\))

solutions.text:
At least \(90\%\) lost means \(0.9^n\le0.1.\) Now \[ \begin{aligned} \log_{10}0.9 &=\log_{10}9-1\\ &=2(0.477)-1\\ &=-0.046. \end{aligned} \] Thus \(n(-0.046)\le-1,\) so \(n\ge21.739\ldots.\) The least integer is \(22.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is E.
hints: After \(n\) years, the fraction of value remaining is \(0.9^n\)
